 NJ Democrats won big on Election Day. Here’s how they did
 By 
 New Jersey Monitor Staff 
 - 
 November 6, 2026 9:11 am 
 People react as results come in on election night during the Rebecca Bennett election night watch party at the Bridgewater Manor on Nov. 3, 2026. (Photo by Anne-Marie Caruso/ New Jersey Monitor)
 New Jersey Democrats had a great Election Day, in case you haven’t already heard.
 They won two GOP-held House seats and won all nine of their own, leaving just one Republican representing New Jersey in the House of Representatives when Congress begins its new term in January.
 Almost all of the votes have been counted in every race, and here’s where they all stand:
 U.S. Senate
 U.S. Sen. Cory Booker (D) won a full third term on Tuesday, winning 62% of the vote. Republican challenger Justin Murphy won 35%.
 Booker’s winning percentage is a bit higher than his last two victories. In 2020, he won 57% and in 2014, 56%. This year was the first time Booker has won Hunterdon and Monmouth counties.
 Sen. Cory Booker speaks at an election eve rally on Nov. 2, 2026, in Springfield. (Photo by Dana DiFIlippo/New Jersey Monitor) 
 U.S. House
 1st District 
 Rep. Donald Norcross (D) won 70% of the vote against Republican challenger Damon Galdo’s 30%.
 2nd District 
 Democrat Zack Mullock, the Cape May mayor, won in a close race against incumbent Rep. Jeff Van Drew (R). Mullock won 51% of the vote to Van Drew’s 48%.
 When Van Drew won reelection in 2024, he won 58% of the vote.
 Zack Mullock appears at a campaign event in Vineland on Nov. 2, 2026. (Photo by Anne-Marie Caruso/New Jersey Monitor) 
 3rd District 
 Rep. Herb Conaway (D) won 63% of the vote in his first bid for reelection. GOP challenger Michael McGuire won 36%.
 4th District 
 The night’s sole Republican winner, Rep. Chris Smith, defeated Democrat Rachel Peace 59%-41%. Two years ago, Smith won 67% of the vote.
 5th District 
 Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D) won 62% of the vote against Republican Sean Kirrane, who won 35%.
 6th District 
 Rep. Frank Pallone (D) defeated Republican Hillary Herzig 69%-31%.
 7th District 
 In the most closely watched race of this cycle, Democrat Rebecca Bennett won 57% to 41% for Rep. Tom Kean Jr. Kean (R) won about 51% the last two times he won in this district.
 Rep.-elect Rebecca Bennett (D) speaks during her victory party in Bridgewater on Nov. 3, 2026. (Photo by Anne-Marie Caruso/New Jersey Monitor) 
 8th District 
 Rep. Rob Menendez (D) had no GOP challenger this year. He won 89% of the vote against three independent candidates.
 9th District 
 Rep. Nellie Pou (D) won her first reelection campaign with 67% of the vote. GOP challenger Rosie Pino won 32%. Two years ago, Pou won 51%.
 10th District 
 Rep. LaMonica McIver (D) won reelection with 85% of the vote. Her Republican challenger, Carmen Bucco, won 16%. When McIver faced Bucco in 2024, she won 74%.
 11th District 
 Rep. Analilia Meji (D) won her first full term against Republican Joe Hathaway 61%-39%. When now-Gov. Mikie Sherrill won this seat in 2024, Sherrill captured 57%.
 12th District 
 First-time candidate Adam Hamawy (D) won 70% of the vote to 28% for Republican opponent Gregg Mele. Hamawy will succeed retiring Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman, who won 61% of the vote in 2024.
 Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, who won New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District on Tuesday, speaks outside the federal courthouse in Newark on Nov. 4, 2026. (Photo by Anne-Marie Caruso/New Jersey Monitor)
